title: HybriMoE: Hybrid CPU-GPU Scheduling and Cache Management for Efficient MoE Inference
problem: MoE inference on resource-constrained hybrid CPU-GPU platforms requires offloading experts, but unstable expert activation patterns and complex workload distribution prevent efficient CPU-GPU scheduling and memory utilization.
motivation: MoE models offer large capacity gains but create uneven compute and memory demands; hybrid platforms can reduce memory pressure if scheduling is adaptive.
method: HybriMoE efficiently runs MoE models (neural networks where different specialized components handle different parts of the task) on CPU-GPU systems. For each layer, it dynamically assigns experts to CPU or GPU based on which ones are actually needed. It also preloads predicted experts for the next layer and prioritizes keeping high-value data in GPU cache.
key_novelty: Instead of using fixed processor-expert assignments, it dynamically changes these for each layer based on real-time usage.
contributions: Dynamic intra-layer scheduling for workload balancing
1.33x-1.70x speedup over SOTA hybrid MoE inference
limitations: Evaluation limited to three MoE-based LLMs; generalization to other MoE architectures or non-MoE models not discussed.
